title: Deep events had a higher M6.5+ share in matched ComCat M5.5+ groups in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether deep earthquakes have a different reported large-event share after location, era and preferred magnitude method are matched. We used a fixed global ComCat snapshot for 2000-2025. The M6.5+ share among M5.5+ events was 8.72% at depths of 0-70 km and 15.63% at depths of 300 km or more. Seventeen matched groups retained 2,948 shallow and 591 deep events. The overlap-weighted deep-minus-shallow difference was 7.40 percentage points. Its conditional 95% three-year block interval was 5.59 to 10.04 points. Planned cell, count, block and cutoff checks gave positive differences. Removing each geographic cell in turn left point differences from 5.79 to 9.32 points. Thus, these matching choices did not remove the catalog association. This is not a physical depth effect, a fitted b-value or a hazard estimate. Preferred methods depend on event size and depth. Limited spatial overlap, selection at the magnitude floor, revised data, and sequence dependence limit inference. Code, aggregate counts, saved draws, source hashes and an independent numerical audit support reproduction. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Reported large-event shares and depth contrasts. Error bars are conditional 95% three-year block intervals. The matched rows use different support sets. Raw point estimates have no error bars.

citations.reason: Prior method-mix result motivated this depth comparison. We reuse its source snapshot, not its code. Observations overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
